_meta.purpose: The durable list of OPEN leads. A lead recorded only in a chat transcript is lost at the next compaction, and a lead recorded only in gen_prompts.py cannot be checked -- nothing in the fleet reports which queue item a job took, so a lead that was tried and failed looks identical to one nobody ever attempted. Each entry below carries a WITNESS: a grep against the live seed tree that matches WHILE THE LEAD IS STILL OPEN. Run check_leads.py to turn 'do we remember this?' into 'is it still in the tree?'.
_meta.usage:
python3 check_leads.py            # status of every lead
python3 check_leads.py --open     # only the ones still open
_meta.status_values: open = witness still matches, nobody has landed it. landed = witness gone, RE-PRICE THE SIBLINGS. unverifiable = no mechanical witness exists; must be checked by hand.
_meta.rule: When a lead flips to landed, do not just delete it -- the pattern that paid once is a reason to CHECK the next instance, never a reason to assume it. Re-derive the siblings against the new tree before requeueing them.
_meta.trees: THREE tree locations, NOT interchangeable. records/<slug>/ is the LEADER's tree, reseeded from whoever holds the record -- this is what jobs are seeded from and therefore what a lead must beat. projs/<slug>/Solution/ is OUR working tree; it equals records/ only on slugs where we lead (on keccak-f1600 ours is theta 3200 against the record's 2240, so reading the wrong one INVERTS the answer). out/<slug>/ is per-job scratch, wiped and re-extracted for the very next job -- a constant read there belongs to whichever job landed last. check_leads.py resolves records/ then projs/ then out/, in that order.
_meta.price_zero: price 0 means UNPRICED, not worthless -- a lead whose mechanism is confirmed but whose row count has not been derived. Derive it before queueing, and write the number back here. Only fb-queue-stale is genuinely a 0 (it is queue hygiene).
_meta.fixed_challenge_rule: THE FIXED-CHALLENGE VACUITY RULE. Our soundness obligation is a Lean theorem `soundness : forall env, constraints_hold env -> spec env` -- unconditional, over ALL witnesses, with no random oracle and no computational assumption. So EVERY published protocol that gets its efficiency from a verifier challenge is unavailable to us in its published form, and the failure is not subtle. Worked out on Wesolowski's proof of exponentiation, whose check is pi^l * g^r = y with l the challenge and r = 2^t mod l public: with l fixed at compile time the prover picks ANY pi and outputs y := pi^l * g^r, which verifies by construction at zero work. Because gcd(l, |G|) = 1 makes pi |-> pi^l g^r a BIJECTION of G, every y has an accepting proof -- the equation is a DEFINITION of y, not a constraint on it, and the gadget proves nothing. Wesolowski's own soundness reduction is to the adaptive root game (output u, THEN receive l, THEN produce v with v^l = u); fixing l reverses the quantifiers and the game is won by sampling v and setting u := v^l. Pietrzak has the identical disease with fixed round challenges, and his footnote 5 records an attack that works merely from omitting y from the hash. GENERALISATION, AND THIS IS THE TEST TO APPLY: given a proposed 'witness the answer, check a relation at a fixed public point' construction, ask whether the check is SURJECTIVE onto the claimed output as the free witness ranges over its domain. If it is, the construction is vacuous. THE ESCAPE, WHEN IT EXISTS: if the relation is a polynomial identity of degree d in the challenge, checking it at d+1 DISTINCT FIXED points forces the identity itself and no challenge is needed -- this is derandomisation, not Fiat-Shamir, and it is sound unconditionally. That is the only route by which any challenge-based protocol enters this cost model. See the ecip-derandomized lead.

_meta.uncatalogued_techniques:
THREE TECHNIQUES THAT WON RECORDS BEFORE THEY WERE WRITTEN DOWN, found by diffing archived record trees 2026-08-11. Between them they account for ALL 340 points of a -60 and a -280. The lesson is that this ledger tracks leads found by ANALYSIS while the fleet banks reductions nobody has catalogued -- so diff the reference/prev-* archives after every record, not just the leads.
T1 CONSTANT-OPERAND COLLAPSE: if every limb of one operand of an interpolated multiply is degree 0, the convolution is affine and the entire <2m-1, 2m-1> witness-and-pin step is deleted. Entry condition is `forall j, degree(b[j]) = 0`, NOT AffineW. See vb-const-operand-collapse.
T3 THE VESTIGIAL ALLOCATION: a gadget that stops constraining its top lane still ALLOCATES it, to keep every downstream offset and localLength lemma working -- and that cell is unconstrained, unread, and CHARGED. It hides because the gadget's own docstring says the allocation is deliberate. THE AUDIT: for every gadget compare `witnessVector n` against the range of the forEach that constrains it and against what the return value reads; any index in neither is free. Cost of collecting it is re-deriving every consumer offset.
T4 THE OFFSET-STABILITY TAX: when a gadget's localLength shrinks, a consumer can re-derive its offsets or swap in a costlier gadget of the OLD length. The second is invisible in a diff -- it looks like a gadget choice, not a cost decision. RULE: whenever a diff both shrinks a constant and swaps a gadget elsewhere, the swap is a deferred debt; record it at the size of the debt or it is never collected. See sha-offset-stability-debt.

leads.note:
CLOSED 2026-08-10 on converging evidence from three independent methods:
(1) THE SLP SEARCH WAS ACTUALLY RUN (tools/theta_slp.py). Boyar-Peralta generalised to 3-input XOR gates over the free module GF(2)^25 (+) GF(2)^25 with rot1 as a shift operator, randomised restarts. Best found h = 35 lane-gates, VERIFIED against a reference Keccak theta. Naive baseline 40. The record is ALSO 35 (records/keccak-f1600/Cost.lean: ThetaC 640 + ThetaXor 1600 = 2240 alloc/round = 35 x 64). The search reproduced the record's own construction and found nothing better -- the winning method it reports is 'absorbed-D', which IS the record's theta-D fusion.
(2) cvc5 QF_FF exact synthesis over BN254 proves parity-5 is UNSAT at one row AND unsat at two rows with one witness (multipliers allowed to vanish). So the 5-way column parity cannot beat two XOR3 in this gadget family -- not a heuristic failure, a proof.
(3) A proposal to drop C and build D directly as a parity-of-10 by free-sum bit extraction (7 score/bit) was arithmetically checked and is 960/round WORSE, not better -- the claim of a 23,040 win had the sign backwards. THE REASON IS THE POINT: the record's output gate is XOR3(A, C[x-1], rot1 C[x+1]), which absorbs BOTH column parities, so D is never materialised and already costs exactly zero. Materialising D can only lose, however cheaply you build it. Record 4480/round vs proposal 5440/round.
WHAT WOULD REOPEN THIS: only a gadget family outside 'one row, one non-vanishing affine multiplier' -- e.g. a 3-row/2-witness gadget emitting TWO C bits jointly. cvc5 can decide that; the generator is reusable. Until then keccak's remaining value is entirely in kec-port-record (122880), not here.
*** THE PROCESS LESSON: this lead was priced at 15360 off a formula, 'score = 153600 + 48h, record h = 640, floor h = 320', that nobody had checked against the tree. h in that formula was ThetaC's per-round ALLOCATIONS (640), while the SLP search's h counts LANE-GATES (35). Two different units, and the 'proved floor of 320' was half of a number that was already optimal. A price derived from a formula is not a price until the units are pinned to a Cost.lean line. ***

*** UPGRADED FROM 'SEARCH FOUND NOTHING' TO A STRUCTURAL OBSTRUCTION, and this is the part worth keeping. ***
The bit-level model was rebuilt from scratch and reproduces the record construction and 184320 EXACTLY, verified against a reference Keccak theta at both bit and 64-bit-word level. So the model is trustworthy and the record is tied, not beaten.
THE COORDINATE SYSTEM: the 320 column-slices form a SINGLE 320-CYCLE under (x,b) -> (x+2, b-1). Each slice-seed is an edge, and the rider of edge n lives in node n+128. Only 320 seeds need construction; the other 1280 targets are free siblings. Anyone attacking this again should start there rather than from the lane picture.
WHY 639 RESISTS, three obstructions, in increasing order of force:
(1) Every count is exactly saturated -- a node has 5 atoms = exactly two fanin-3 gates (3, then +2), and a target has weight 11 = exactly rider + P + P = 3 slots. There is no slack anywhere to absorb a saved gate.
(2) Every shortcut is circular: C[x][b] = T xor rider xor C[x+2][b-1] is one helper, but that target itself needs C[x][b]. Every relation of this shape closes on itself.
(3) THE DECISIVE ONE, AND IT IS A MODULAR INVARIANT, NOT A SEARCH RESULT. The 3-column 9->8 repair that motivated this whole lead WAS reproduced and verified -- and then decoded: node 2's parity costs only one helper because two of its five atoms arrive free as riders of already-built targets, one cancelled by a neighbour's dirty wire. That mechanism requires the rider offset k on the node cycle to be <= 2. MEASURED: 3-column w=1 has k = 2, so it works. EVERY 5-column instance has k == 3 (mod 5): w=1 -> 3, w=2 -> 8, w=4 -> 8, w=64 -> 128. Since 3 is not 0, 1 or 2 mod 5, THE COINCIDENCE CANNOT OCCUR FOR KECCAK THETA AT ANY LANE WIDTH.
MATCHING NEGATIVE SEARCHES (seeded from the record, delete one helper, anneal to repair, helpers allowed to consume produced targets): 5-node cycle 10->9 failed over 367 restarts; 10-node 20->19 failed; 20-node 40->39 failed -- each stuck at exactly 10 unresolved targets, the two slices flanking the crippled node. The 3-node cycle repaired in 49 restarts. So the 3-column result is a genuine FALSE FRIEND: it is real, it is verified, and it does not generalise.
WHAT IS LEFT, IF ANYTHING: the search held lanes uniform, which is a self-imposed constraint the real bit-level problem does not require. Any win must be a NON-UNIFORM bit-level scheme that breaks the k == 3 (mod 5) invariant or routes around it. The corpus's h >= 320 floor claim is untouched by this work and the 320-to-640 gap is real, but no mechanism crossing it was found.
MY OWN BRIEF WAS WRONG ON THE UNITS AND THE AGENT HAD TO RECONCILE IT: I wrote 'standing record is h = 640, even h = 639 is a record'. Under the literal lane-level rules the textbook schedule is 40 gates, so 'beat 640' would be trivial. The challenge is BIT-level: score = 153600 + 48h with h counting HELPER gates only, the 1600 target Xor3 rows already sitting inside the 153600 base, and the record h = 640 = 320 column-slices x 2 helpers. Writing a brief in the wrong units nearly wasted the whole run.
ARTIFACTS: tools/theta_slp.py (lane SLP + searches), tools/theta_bits.py (bit-level model + record verification), tools/theta_repair.py (the decisive repair search), tools/theta_anneal.py, tools/theta_slp_result.json, tools/repair_3_1.json.
THE FOUR ANALOGUES, WITH THEIR EVIDENCE STRENGTH STATED HONESTLY (cols/w -> node cycle, rider offset k, h-1 repair result): 3/1 -> 3, k=2, REPAIRED in 49 restarts. 5/1 -> 5, k=3, failed over 367 restarts. 5/2 -> 10, k=8, failed over 62 restarts. 5/4 -> 20, k=8, failed -- BUT THIS LAST ROW IS THE WEAKEST POINT: the run was killed once the pattern was established, and its label comes from an earlier 60-second pass that recorded the deletion as unrepaired after only 16 deletions tried. Treat 5/4 as suggestive, not established. The invariant argument, not the search, is what closes this lead.

Best parametrisation needs 4n+10 FIXED LINES, i.e. 14 for a single-point MSM -- not the 'under 10' hoped for but far under the 49 of the published form. *** VACUITY, SETTLED EMPIRICALLY. *** With A0 fixed at compile time the check is SURJECTIVE onto Q. Concrete forgery: set b=0, a_den=1, a_num=c0+c1*x (inside the allowed degree bounds); the check collapses to ONE linear equation c0*(coeff0-coeff2) + c1*(coeff0*u - coeff2*x2) = rho in two unknowns, so every claimed Q has an accepting witness. Verified: 200/200 random wrong Q forged, zero circuit work. So single-point ECIP is vacuous, not merely unproven. Confirms _meta.fixed_challenge_rule.

*** THE DERANDOMISATION COUNT, DERIVED. *** The identity is a rational function of the challenge; force it by evaluating at deg+1 fixed points. Measured degrees (three parametrisations, all verified numerically against a genuine garaga witness on secp256k1):
  (a) garaga's published TANGENT form (A2 = -2*A0, parametrise by x_A0): needs 20n+29 distinct x-coordinates, each used at both +-v. n=1 -> 49. The blow-up is the composition with [-2], a degree-4 map.
  (b) MY REFORMULATION, pencil of lines through a FIXED auxiliary point A1 (so A2 = -(A0+A1), a degree-1 map): 10n+21. n=1 -> 31. Derived by differentiating Weil reciprocity along that family; verified 10/10 against garaga's honest witness.
  (c) BEST: Eagen's own MIXED form (his eval_function_challenge_mixed) derandomised over the PENCIL OF PARALLEL LINES y = m x + b, m fixed at compile time, b the parameter. The three intersection points are conjugate over F_p(b), so the LHS is a FIELD TRACE and the whole identity is a rational function of the single parameter b. Verified 12/12 on secp256k1 with m fixed. Count: 6n+12 lines. n=1 -> 18.
  (d) (c) PLUS a common-denominator witness encoding: garaga's a_den always DIVIDES b_den (verified 18/18 across n=1,2,4), so witness (a_num deg n+3, b_num deg n+1, D deg n+4) with alpha=a_num/D, beta=b_num/D. Then 4n+10 lines. n=1 -> 14, n=2 -> 18, n=4 -> 26.
EXACT LAW, verified by sweeping each degree independently: deg_b(Phi) = 2*deg(denominator) + (#basis points). NUMERATOR degrees cost NOTHING. So the only lever left is shrinking the denominator.

*** THE COST MODEL WAS ALSO WRONG, IN OUR FAVOUR. *** The '~89 F_p multiplications per evaluation' figure assumed a witnessed A0. When A0 (or the line) is a COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT, x_A2, y_A2, the coefficients, the slope/intercept and every power x_i^t are constants, so evaluating a witnessed-coefficient polynomial at them is a FREE AFFINE FORM. Per line the only rows are the DIVISIONS: 3 (one per intersection point, common-denominator encoding) + 1 per basis point. n=1: ~6 mulmods/line, or ~9 with explicit nonzero certificates. 14 lines x 9 = ~126 certified F_p multiplications, against ~364 for the current 4-dim GLV lattice design.

*** WHY IT IS STILL NOT ACTIONABLE, AND THESE ARE THE BLOCKERS TO ATTACK IN ORDER. *** (1) The converse -- 'identity holds in b => (ep-en)P = Q' -- is Eagen's theorem and I could NOT fetch the paper (eprint 403). I verified only the forward direction numerically. Everything above prices a theorem we have not read. (2) Eagen's own notebook warns verbatim: 'if the scalars can exceed field length protocol can fail to be sound', and his demo uses scalars HALF the field length. Our ep, en are 251/255 bits on a 256-bit field. If the half-length restriction is real, GLV-split first: n=2, 18 lines, ~198 mulmods -- still under 364, so the lead survives either way. (3) ep and en enter the circuit as F_p elements but must be INTEGERS for the divisor argument, so they carry integer range obligations (ep-en = k holds over Z, verified: exactly, at 8/64/255 bits). (4) THE ACTUAL KILLER FOR THIS PIPELINE: the Lean soundness theorem would need Weil reciprocity, divisors and principality on an elliptic curve. Mathlib has the group law via the class group but nothing like the function-field machinery this needs. That is a multi-month formalisation, and Aristotle will not produce it. NEXT STEP, and it is cheap: get eprint 2022/596 by any route (author homepage, a mirror, a citing thesis) and read the soundness theorem's exact hypotheses. Everything else is priced.

leads.note: GENERAL TECHNIQUE, NOT A SITE -- applies to every degree-2 certificate in every tree, which is most of them. The mechanism: diagonalising a quadratic form is a free change of basis because affine combinations cost nothing, and each hyperbolic pair collapses two squares into ONE product. If c^2 = -b/a is a non-residue, mix in a third index; Chevalley-Warning guarantees isotropy for r >= 3, so the pairing never gets stuck. Combined with 'never assert your last equation' (II.11) the emit is ceil(r/2) rows and ceil(r/2)-1 witnesses. FIRST MOVE: take one existing degree-2 certificate whose relation has visible rank above 2 -- the GroupedEq family is the obvious candidate -- compute the rank of its symmetric matrix, and see whether ceil(r/2) is below what it currently pays. leads.summary: Deterministic permutation / multiset-equality certificate with NO random challenge: a Waksman network of 1-row switches. Cost 2(n log2 n - n + 1) score. n=64 -> 642, n=1024 -> 18434.
leads.note: THE SWITCH IS THE NEW PART AND IT IS WORTH KNOWING ON ITS OWN. The textbook selector out1 = a + s(b-a) with s boolean costs 2 rows + 2 witnesses. Instead witness ONLY out1 and assert (out1 - a)(out1 - b) = 0, then take out2 = a + b - out1 as a free affine. That pins {out1,out2} = {a,b} as a MULTISET in one row and one witness. Waksman's network realises every permutation in S_n with n log2 n - n + 1 such switches, so the constraint variety is exactly {(x, pi(x))} -- no challenge, no grand product, and therefore expressible as an unconditional Lean soundness theorem, which the grand-product argument is NOT. NOTHING IN THE CURRENT FIVE CHALLENGES NEEDS THIS. Recorded because it is the correct answer to sorting, RAM, and set-equality if one ever appears, and because the 1-row two-root switch is a I.4-family gadget (decoy roots) we did not have.

leads.summary: n-ary XOR of booleans: for n >= 7 extract the parity from the FREE sum instead of building an XOR3 tree. Witness the m = ceil(log2(floor(n/2)+1)) bits of q, assert (s-2q)(s-2q-1) = 0; parity is the free affine s-2q. Cost 2m+1 vs 2*ceil((n-1)/2).
leads.note: Crossover is at n=7 (tree 6 vs free-sum 5); it widens fast -- n=15 gives 14 vs 7, n=31 gives 30 vs 9, n=63 gives 62 vs 11. Linear becomes logarithmic. SOUNDNESS: q is a genuine integer in [0, 2^m - 1] via its own bits, and s - 2q in {0,1} forces q = floor(s/2) uniquely; a superset range is safe whenever 2q+1 > n is unreachable. NOT APPLICABLE TO KECCAK THETA -- its widest XOR is the 5-way column parity, which is below the crossover, and see keccak-theta-slp for why materialising anything wider loses. The general form is Paterson-Stockmeyer: any SYMMETRIC boolean function is a univariate in the free sum s, evaluable in about 2*sqrt(n) products (m non-scalar mults reach degree floor((m+2)^2/4)). Look for symmetric subfunctions before building trees. NEGATIVE WORTH KEEPING: generic bit-packing into base-8/base-13 digits of one field element never helps, because the unpacking identity was ALREADY free and packing forces you to witness digits that were free affine forms. That is distinct from I.2 lambda-packing, which is genuine but needs the packed output consumed additively.

leads.summary: Rewrite Sigma0/Sigma1/sigma0/sigma1 in carry-save form and never materialise them. A+B+C = (A xor B xor C) + 2*maj(A,B,C) over the integers, so each becomes a FREE integer affine combination of rotations minus twice a majority word.
leads.source: SHA-256 reformulation research, 2026-08-10, verified on 1e5 random inputs per function and on 1e5 full-round states
leads.note: COST-NEUTRAL BY ITSELF -- a maj bit and an xor3 bit are both <1,1>, and maj = (s - xor3)/2 with s free, so they are affinely interchangeable. ITS VALUE IS AS A PRECONDITION: it is what makes sha-sigma-trunc's free top bit exist, it enables sha-shr-pack, and it deletes four 32-bit intermediate words per round from the witness. The fused round becomes e' == d + h + K + W + [ROTR6+ROTR11+ROTR25](e) + Ch(e,f,g) - 2N1 (mod 2^32), and a' the same plus [ROTR2+ROTR13+ROTR22](a) + Maj(a,b,c) - 2N0. Sigma0, Sigma1, T1 and T2 are never materialised; the whole nonlinearity of a round is three majority words and one Ch word. FIRST STEP: prove in Lean that A + B + C = (A ^^^ B ^^^ C) + 2 * maj A B C over Nat restricted to < 2^32, then rewrite the round to emit N0, N1 and fold the rotation sums into the existing free linear combination.

leads.summary: The SHR positions of sigma0/sigma1 feed compile-time ZEROS, so their gadgets degenerate from degree 3 to degree 2 -- maj(A,B,0) = A AND B, xor3(A,B,0) = A XOR B -- and degree-2 gadgets pack TWO per row. sigma0 positions 29-30 and sigma1 positions 22-30.
leads.note: 5 rows per schedule step, 240 per block. THE UNDERLYING DICHOTOMY IS THE REUSABLE PART AND IT IS PROVED: a gadget's MULTILINEAR DEGREE over the boolean cube decides everything. Degree 2 (Ch, XOR2, AND2) takes the C-slot shape gamma*z = P0*Q0 - R0 and packs EXACTLY 2 per row -- never 3, because for k gadgets on disjoint variables the quadratic form is a direct sum of k rank->=1 blocks and the C-slot shape needs rank <= 2 modulo the free diagonal shifts. Degree 3 (Maj, XOR3, AND3) takes the non-vanishing-multiplier shape and packs NEVER -- proved, including against decoy roots, by applying the bi-non-affine projector: z^2 contributes 2*lambda*f~ (x) g~ which nothing else in the row can match. Exhaustive search over multipliers with coefficients in [-3,3] agrees: zero hits for MAJ+MAJ, XOR3+XOR3, XOR3+MAJ, MAJ+CH, AND3+MAJ, including pairs sharing one or two inputs. SO: stop looking for a row that packs two Maj or two XOR3. That search is closed. circomlib captures part of this (its O1 pass kills mid = b*c for 13 bits per SigmaPlus, 624 constraints) but neither the packing of the surviving degree-2 gadgets nor the free top bit appears in any implementation found.

leads.summary: The message-schedule quotient is exactly 2 bits. Machine-checked over 2e5 random 4-tuples: q_i in {0,1,2,3}, and it follows immediately because after the -2n corrections all four terms are genuine 32-bit words so their sum is < 4*2^32.
leads.note: CHECK WHAT WE CURRENTLY CHARGE BEFORE PRICING THIS -- if MessageSchedule.lean already witnesses 2 bits the item is worth zero; if it charges 3 bits or a product chain, replace with two witnessed bits and let the reduction row absorb q = q0 + 2*q1 for free. The whole schedule step is one free affine form plus two majority words plus this quotient: the bracketed rotation/shift sum plus W[i-7] plus W[i-16] is ENTIRELY FREE, and the only nonlinearity is -2*n1(W[i-2]) - 2*n0(W[i-15]). Carries cannot be shared across words -- each W feeds exactly one sigma0 and one sigma1 in its lifetime and the majority words of different steps have disjoint variable sets. NEGATIVE WORTH KEEPING: the SHA-2 cryptanalysis literature on the linearised schedule (Rijmen-Oswald, Pramstaller et al., Matusiewicz-Pieprzyk, Mendel et al.) does NOT hand us this decomposition -- it replaces + by XOR and studies the code's minimum weight, discarding the carry correction as the thing that makes linearisation approximate. That is the term we need.

leads.summary: CLOSED DIRECTIONS, recorded so they are not re-explored. Sparse/spread representation, meet-in-the-middle, alternative rotation-friendly representations, and rank/tensor diagonalisation of the Sigma words are all dead, each for a structural reason.
leads.note: (1) SPARSE/SPREAD (halo2 table16, 2099 rows) -- the ENTIRE saving is that the dense<->spread bijection is one LOOKUP row. Enforcing it arithmetically means decomposing the 16-bit chunk into bits and re-summing with weights 4^i, i.e. back to >=1 row per bit. No lookup-free variant exists or can. (2) MEET-IN-THE-MIDDLE -- the backward round invokes the IDENTICAL four nonlinear gadgets on the identical words; the bijection is realised entirely by free affine rearrangement, so direction does not touch the nonlinear content. Zero gain, and note the feed-forward is NOT what blocks it. (3) ROTATION-FRIENDLY REPRESENTATIONS (roots of unity in F_r, F_2[x]/(x^32-1)) -- every invertible linear change of representation is free in BOTH directions, so it cannot change the cost of anything. The bit vector already has rotation free AND addition free; the only cost is re-decomposition, which is intrinsic to the nonlinear interface. (4) RANK/TENSOR DIAGONALISATION of the Sigma words -- the quadratic part is rank <= 32 and would give 16 rows, but the cubic part T = sum 2^j x_{j+u} x_{j+v} x_{j+w} is a DIAGONAL 3-tensor with 32 nonzero entries, slice rank exactly 32, so >= ceil(32/3) = 11 multiplications for T alone and realistically 32. THE LESSON: the non-vanishing-multiplier row is extraordinarily good precisely because it computes a degree-3 function in ONE row by hiding the degree in a division. Rank methods must pay for degree 3 explicitly and cannot compete. (5) A GENUINE BUT SMALL ITEM, not a dead end: for the FIRST block the state is the constant IV, so round 0's gadgets are compile-time constants and at round 1 both Maj and Ch have two constant arguments and collapse to free affine functions. Worth about 2 rounds on block 1 only.

leads.summary: The grand-product permutation argument IS derandomisable without a challenge, and the naive way to do it is quadratic while the right way is n*log2(n) - n/4 - 1 products.
leads.source: Derived 2026-08-11 in the verification-identities pass; libsnark AS-Waksman sources fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com; Newton's identities and Shurman's resultant notes fetched.
leads.note: prod_i(a_i+g) = prod_i(b_i+g) with g fixed is ONE equation in n free unknowns -> the prover solves for b_n -> VACUOUS, exactly the Wesolowski disease. But both sides are monic of degree n in g, so the difference has degree <= n-1 and checking at n DISTINCT FIXED points forces the identity unconditionally. The trap: evaluating prod_i(x_j - b_i) separately at each of n points costs n^2-n products. The fix: build the product by a BINARY TREE, and at each node multiply two monic degree-d polynomials by the 2d+1-fixed-point evaluate/multiply/interpolate route (evaluation of a witnessed-coefficient polynomial at a compile-time point is a FREE affine form; only the pointwise products are rows). Naive convolution wins for d<=2, evaluation for d>=3, giving C(n) = n*log2(n) - n/4 - 1 products; verified by direct recursion at n=4..1024 (C(8)=21, C(16)=59, C(64)=367, C(256)=1983). Score against a PUBLIC multiset = 2n*log2(n) - n/2 - 4; both sides witnessed = 4n*log2(n) - n - 8. Compare Waksman with libsnark's boolean-ELIMINATED switch (o1-u)(o1-v)=0 (1 row, 1 alloc, NOT the 2-row boolean form): 2(n*log2(n) - n + 1), about 15% cheaper. Two unrelated derandomisations landing on the same 2n*log2(n) is good evidence that is the true price of a challenge-free permutation. The product tree is much easier to prove in Lean (one Vandermonde uniqueness lemma + a tree induction) than Waksman's routability.

leads.summary: Rows are charged per multiplication and nothing else, so the row count of any bilinear map is its TENSOR RANK. Strassen is therefore a free lunch in R1CS with crossover at n=2, not n~100.
leads.source: Derived 2026-08-11; Strassen exponent and Winograd addition counts fetched from Wikipedia.
leads.note: Every non-multiplicative step of a bilinear algorithm -- the block adds, the change of basis, the reassembly -- is affine and therefore FREE, so the R1CS cost of a bilinear map is exactly its bilinear rank. Same theorem as the Winograd 2n-k bound for F[u]/P already in CIRCONOMICON I.10, stated for the matrix-multiplication tensor. Consequence: n^3 -> 7^log2(n). n=8: 512 -> 343 (33%); n=16: 4096 -> 2401 (41%); n=64: 262144 -> 117649 (55%). Each leaf product is (affine form in A) x (affine form in B), a legal rank-1 row. The numerical-stability and addition-overhead objections that push Strassen's classical crossover to n~100 are all costs this model does not charge. Laderman R(3,3,3)<=23 and AlphaTensor-style decompositions would push further -- UNVERIFIED, not fetched, do not quote numbers without a decomposition in hand.

leads.summary: A chi output bit costs ONE R1CS row with output booleanity FREE, and a 3-way parity costs ONE row. That is theta 2240 rows (not 6400) and chi 5 rows per 5-bit row (not 10).

leads.note:
*** CROSS-CHECKED AGAINST THE LIVE TREES AND IT IS AN INDEPENDENT REDISCOVERY OF THE RECORD'S OWN CONSTRUCTION, WHICH IS THE BEST POSSIBLE OUTCOME FOR THE PORT. *** This was derived from first principles without reading the record, and it lands on the record's exact numbers: records/keccak-f1600/Cost.lean:87 proves ThetaC <640,640>, :91 proves ThetaXor <1600,1600> (sum 2240, matching the derived theta figure exactly), and :78 proves ChiLane <64,64>, i.e. one row per bit across 64 bits. THE ACTION IS UNCHANGED: this is already queued as the port ladder, Rung A (ChiLane alone, -76,800) then Rung B then Rung C. Do NOT open a separate line of work on it.

chi: (4a'_i - 3a_i + a_{i+1} + a_{i+2}) * (2a_i - 2a_{i+1} - 2a_{i+2} + 1) = 3a_i - a_{i+1} - 5a_{i+2}. The right factor takes values in {1,-1,-1,-3,3,1,1,-1} on the cube -- NEVER ZERO -- so a'_i is uniquely pinned to a boolean and its booleanity costs 0. Verified on all 8 inputs. Needs char not in {2,3}. parity-of-3: (2o - s)(2s - 3) = -s with s = x+y+z, right factor in {-3,-1,1,3}. parity-of-2: (o + 2s)(s + 1) = 6s. The parity-3 gadget works for ANY affine form provably valued in [0,3], so parity cost rho(k) = min(ceil(log2(k+1)), 1 + rho(k-2)); crossover at k=7. THETA REBUILT: share the column parities. C[x][z] = parity of 5 -> 2 rows, 320*2 = 640; then each output bit = parity of 3 -> 1 row, 1600. Total 2240 rows/theta, 2.9x under the naive 4-rows-per-bit 6400. Full Keccak-f1600 budget on this basis: 1600 + 24*2240 + 24*1600 = 93,760 rows = 93,760 allocs, score ~187,520. CHECK THIS AGAINST THE LIVE TREE BEFORE SPENDING A SLOT -- it may already be in.
INVERSES ARE DEAD, with the reason: computed theta and theta^-1 over GF(2) by Gauss-Jordan -- EVERY row of theta has weight exactly 11, EVERY row of theta^-1 has weight exactly 851 (density 0.5319), confirming the Keccak reference's 'Hamming weight of the polynomial of theta^-1 is of the order b/2'. 16,000 rows vs 2240, 7.1x worse. chi^-1 = a'_i XOR (~a'_{i+1} AND (a'_{i+2} XOR (~a'_{i+3} AND a'_{i+4}))) = two chi-shaped layers, F_r multilinear degree 5, and it provably admits NO one-row certificate (the required cofactor is forced to a multiple of a'_{i+1}, which vanishes on the cube) -> 10 rows, exactly 2x. AND MEET-IN-THE-MIDDLE IS A NO-OP, NOT A LOSS: R1CS asserts a relation, not a function; witnessing a midpoint and 'running backward' emits character-for-character the same constraints. Inversion pays only when a component is expensive forward and cheap backward; Keccak has no such component.

leads.summary: Composing two SHA-256 rounds saves EXACTLY ZERO (788 = 788), and folding the message schedule's carries COSTS 39. Both closed with explicit counts.
leads.source: Derived 2026-08-11; circomlib ch.circom and sha256compression.circom fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com; verified against real 2-round SHA-256 on 2000 random states.
leads.note: TWO-ROUND COMPOSITION: 2 rounds separately = <392,396> = 788. Composed, including every obligation the composition still forces = <392,396> = 788. IDENTICAL. Reason, and it generalises: E = e_{t+1} and A = a_{t+1} are the ARGUMENTS OF BITWISE MAPS (Sigma1/Ch read E bitwise, Sigma0/Maj read A bitwise), so their 32-bit decompositions are mandatory however you write the relation. Composition raises the symbolic degree but R1CS caps every row at degree 2, so flattening puts back exactly the rows composition removed. Composition here is anti-flattening followed by an undo. a_{t+1} - e_{t+1} = T2_t - d_t IS affine and true mod 2^32 (verified) but is LITERALLY R2 - R1 of the two reduction relations -- linearly dependent, zero new information, and materialising T1 to 'exploit the sharing' costs +63/round. The GF(2) AND-count rewrites INVERT SIGN over F_r: Ch = g^(e&(f^g)) is <3,3>/bit against <1,1>/bit for g + e(f-g); Maj = (a&b)^(c&(a^b)) is <4,4>/bit against <1,1>/bit for the MAJ3 row. 3x and 4x worse -- do not port AND-count results into this model. MESSAGE SCHEDULE: the generating-function collapse dies twice -- sigma0 is not multiplication by any constant of F_r (the rotate's wraparound depends on the low bits), and a truncated power-series identity is 48 coefficient equations, collapsing which is Schwartz-Zippel. The carry fold: |R_t| < 2^34 so B = 2^35, and 35m - 1 < 253.597 gives EXACTLY 7 steps foldable per relation. But it LOSES: the per-step linking relation is already a ring identity costing 0 rows, and each independent linear relation is worth exactly one free derived witness, so folding 46 relations into 7 costs +39 allocations and saves 0 rows. 8650 -> 8689. ALSO: CIRCONOMICON I.2 claims 128 score per round pair for lambda-packing; only 64 (the Ch pair) could be substantiated -- Maj provably does not pack in the I.2 shape (surviving degree-3 ANF terms) and an exhaustive integer search over the I.1 shape (759,375 candidates) came back empty. POSSIBLE OVER-CLAIM IN OUR OWN NOTES -- re-derive before relying on it.

leads.summary: Additive folding works at the LIMB level, not the relation level, and only after the limb products are replaced by a 2k-1-point FIXED-evaluation check. Worth 39.6% per modmul. Everything multiplicative dies.
leads.source: Derived 2026-08-11 with exact integer bit budgets; xJsnark PDF (akosba.github.io/papers/xjsnark.pdf) and gnark std/math/emulated/field_mul.go fetched.
leads.note:
KEEP TWO SOUNDNESS ARGUMENTS STRICTLY APART. (L) magnitude lift: U = V mod r plus |U|,|V| < r/2 gives U = V over Z -- a no-wraparound argument, NOT Schwartz-Zippel, and every use needs an explicit bit budget. (V) Vandermonde: two polynomials of degree <= D agreeing at D+1 FIXED distinct public points are identical -- deterministic, zero soundness error. gnark's mulCheck uses the FORBIDDEN thing (its own comment: 'checked only at a single random point', challenge from a commitment) -- unusable here. xJsnark uses (V): 'For each c in {1..2m-1}, the circuit checks (sum x[i]c^i)(sum y[i]c^i) = sum z[i]c^i ... total number of constraints is 2m-1'. That is the purest form of check-don't-compute and it is legal.
DEAD: multiplicative telescoping (k folded squarings need a quotient of ~4096*2^k bits; k=16 is 268,431,361 bits, and the optimum is k=1 -- enforced at k=2 not by the quotient, which is a literal tie at 16,385 vs 16,386 bits, but by the limb-product count, 1.82x worse). DEAD: relation-level additive folding (residuals are 8193 bits, B > 2^8194, and floor(254/8194) = 0 relations fold -- you would need a 139,281-bit field). DEAD: RNS/CRT auxiliary moduli (1.85x worse; a CRT modulus certifies ~111 bits at 2.5 score/bit while a positional fold chunk certifies b*g bits at 0.25 score/bit, because the carry is NARROWER than the window it certifies while the RNS quotient is WIDER than its modulus; and Mersenne moduli are impossible -- the primes up to 126 sum to 1,593 bits < 8,194).
ALIVE: overlapping-weight limb folding, g_max(b) = floor((252 - ceil(lg k) - 2)/b) - 1. b=64 folds exactly 2, b=20 folds 11. Combined optimum b=20, k=205, g=11: 20,132 score/modmul against 33,351, a 39.6% saving, chain 342,244. AND THE LOAD-BEARING WARNING: for an ARBITRARY residual vector every chunk equation is satisfiable mod p by C_j = S_j * (2^{bg})^{-1}, with forged carries 250-253 bits wide -- the chunk rows are VACUOUS on their own and the entire soundness content is the 28-bit carry RANGE CHECK. Any fold without a bound is unsound. RESIDUE: 278,562 of the final 342,244 (81.4%) is range checks on q and t, at a provable 2 score/bit for the whole digit-decomposition family (one row at most doubles degree, so d bits need >= d rows; the base-4 gadget (y^2-y)(y^2-5y+6)=0 ties booleanity, it does not beat it). A sub-2-score-per-bit range argument is worth more than every structural trick above combined.

leads.summary: Elliptic nets / division polynomials / Somos lose to windowed fixed-base double-and-add by 20-30x, and a fixed base buys them ~0%. Closed with sourced numbers. Pairings on secp256k1 are not merely expensive, they are not representable.
leads.source: Stange thesis (katestange.net/colorado/papers/Stange-Thesis-Brown2008.pdf) and EDS formulary (katestange.net/colorado/papers/edsformulary.pdf) FETCHED and quoted; counts reproduced by an operation-counting implementation checked against real secp256k1 scalar multiplication.
leads.note: Real per-bit cost is 22M + 6S + 4 const-M (Stange's own optimised block algorithm, thesis 18.4), rising to 24M + 6S + 4 const-M + 8 selects in-circuit because the scalar is secret -- 2-3x worse than the 12-16/bit folklore figure. Cross-checks against her Table 18.1. The 8-term block (thesis Thm 19.2.5) is provably minimal: width b supports b-4 values of i giving 2(b-4) new terms, and 2b-8 >= b forces b >= 8. Point recovery x(kP) = x(P) - W(k-1)W(k+1)/W(k)^2 and y(kP) = (W(k+2)W(k-1)^2 - W(k-2)W(k+1)^2)/(4y(P)W(k)^3), ~13 mulmods once, negligible. FIXED BASE BUYS NOTHING: only the initial block and the 4 constant multipliers are compile-time; the block after t steps depends on the whole t-bit prefix, so nothing downstream is constant, and precomputing 2^t initial blocks needs a 2^t-way decoder that eats the gain. Stange's own escape -- 'if W(2,0) has a cube root nu in F_q ... saving four F_q multiplications per iteration' -- is UNAVAILABLE on secp256k1: p = 1 mod 3 and 2*y_G is not a cube mod p (checked). TOTALS: 255 steps x 34 mulmod-equivalents ~ 8,200-8,700 mulmods ~ 41k-70k rows, against ~2,200-2,700 rows for 4-bit-window fixed-base affine addition (63 additions x 3 certified mulmods -- note the affine add is 3, not 5: lam*(x2-x1) = y2-y1, lam*lam = x3+x1+x2, lam*(x1-x3) = y3+y1, all RHS affine and free). 0.75 mulmods/bit against 34. Nets are inherently bit-serial -- Stange, thesis 18.4: 'A triple-and-add adaptation ... does not seem promising, by the nature of the recurrence relation.' Division polynomials are the SAME algorithm (W_n = lambda^(n^2-1) psi_n) with the same count; Somos-4 is the same sequence reached by an O(n) traversal. All three dead. EMBEDDING DEGREE of secp256k1 = ord_n(p) = (n-1)/6 = 254 bits exactly (computed and minimality-checked against every prime divisor of k). F_{p^k} has ~5e78 bits. Pairings do not exist in any computational sense -- every pairing-based verification identity is dead on arrival.

leads.summary: With a deterministic verifier, dIP = NP: there is no protocol to find, only an NP certificate to golf. The right literature is CERTIFYING ALGORITHMS, not SNARKs. Prefer certificates whose verification condition is LINEAR, because linear is free.

leads.note: Katz, verbatim: 'if the verifier is deterministic then the prover can predict all the verifier's questions in advance, and simply include all the corresponding answers as part of the (static) proof.' Our Lean obligation IS a deterministic verifier. So sumcheck, GKR, PCP, KZG, Bulletproofs, plookup/logUp, Wesolowski/Pietrzak are all dead as protocols and useful only as sources of algebraic identities to be derandomised at deg+1 fixed points. THE PATTERN WORTH INTERNALISING is Farkas: the certificate for a NO answer is often a linear functional, and linear functionals are free. Non-solvability of Ax=b is witnessed by c with c^T A = 0 (n^2 FREE affine equations) and c^T b != 0 (one nonzero-certificate row) -- 2 rows total. Same shape for LP infeasibility, min-cut, and Koenig's |M| = |C|. 2-colourability of a compile-time graph is <n,n> regardless of |E| because b_u + b_v - 1 = 0 is affine. Planarity via f - e + n = 2 is a counting identity, i.e. affine, i.e. free. THE DETERMINANT HIERARCHY, worth knowing before paying: det A = 0 costs n^2 (a null vector); det A != 0 costs n^{log2 7} (witness B, assert AB = I -- one-sided suffices over a field, do not pay for both); det A = d costs (n^3-n)/3 + n - 1 (witnessed LU). Ask which you need. NOTE A*adj(A) = d*I is NOT a valid certificate for det A = d -- with the adjugate free it only gives det A * det B = d^n, which fails the vacuity test. RANK EXACTLY r without index selection: A = XY (rank <= r) AND UAV = I_r (rank >= r, since rank(UAV) <= rank(A)); dodges the one-hot decodes a named minor would cost. SQUARE ROOT, the sharpest single lesson: s*s = x is 1 row and a ~380x win when you do not care WHICH root, and a NET LOSS when you do -- pinning the canonical root needs a canonical bit-decomposition plus a comparison against (r-1)/2, ~760 score, more than the ~380 rows of just exponentiating. And if BOTH s and x are free witnesses the check says only 'x is a square' -- that is the vacuous configuration. LEGENDRE SYMBOL in 4 rows: b(b-1) = 0, x*u = 1, t = x*(1 + b*(nu-1)), s*s = t with nu a compile-time non-residue; exactly one of b = 0, b = 1 is satisfiable, so b is forced. The x*u = 1 row is not optional -- without it x = 0 admits both. ORDER IS NEVER ALGEBRAIC: every <, min, sorted, median costs a range check, and witnessing only moves WHICH value gets range-checked, never how many bits. Sorting networks are strictly dominated by log2(n)^2/4 -- witness the sorted array, certify the permutation, pay n-1 comparisons instead of (n/4)log^2(n) of them (n=64,k=32: 4,611 against 36,864). ELIMINATION, the cross-cutting rule and its exception: in R1CS intermediate witnesses are CHEAP (alloc + row = 2, flat) and eliminating them RAISES DEGREE, which is the opposite of the classical instinct. Resultants multiply degrees (Shurman: the resultant is homogeneous of degree mn in the roots), so eliminating n variables from degree-d relations gives degree ~d^n. Chain of monomials: a wash. Boolean selector: elimination WINS -- y = b*u + (1-b)*v costs 4, while (y-u)(y-v) = 0 costs 1, and generally y in {c_1..c_k} for compile-time constants is k-1 rows and 0 allocations against >= 2k. Branching chain: elimination is a DISASTER, 4n against Omega(2^n). Rule: eliminate a boolean selector, never eliminate through a chain.
